items.stem: Mention two features of the life of the native peoples of North America.
items.answer: Lived in groups along river valleys; grew maize and vegetables; hunted bison; did not claim ownership of land; exchanged goods as gifts.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Lived in groups along river valleys; grew maize and vegetables; hunted bison; did not claim ownership of land; exchanged goods as gifts.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Settlers wanted native land.
items.answer: They wished to establish farms and settlements as private property.

items.stem: The following statement about Europeans and the native peoples of North America is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The natives of North America claimed private ownership of land."
items.answer: They did not claim ownership of land and used only what they needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (They did not claim ownership of land and used only what they needed.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: How did the Europeans and the natives view each other?
items.answer: Europeans saw natives as uncivilised, lazy and to be civilised or removed; natives saw Europeans as greedy for land and goods; different ideas about land and trade.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Europeans saw natives as uncivilised, lazy and to be civilised or removed; natives saw Europeans as greedy for land and goods; different ideas about land and trade.

items.stem: "The beaver population declined in North America." Examine this statement with reference to Europeans and the native peoples of North America.
items.answer: The statement is valid. The fur trade with Europeans encouraged excessive hunting.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the fur trade with Europeans encouraged excessive hunting.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

Read the following extract on the native peoples of Australia and terra nullius and answer the questions that follow.
"The British claimed that Australia was terra nullius, empty land, and took it without treaties. Australia was used by Britain as a penal colony, and convicts were sent there from 1788. The natives lost their land to sheep farms and later to mining and settlement."
(i) Children of mixed descent taken from Aboriginal families are known as the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Aborigines' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Many Aboriginal children grew up without their families. (2)
items.answer: (i) stolen generations (ii) The native peoples of Australia, from the Latin 'ab origine', meaning 'from the beginning'. (iii) The government forcibly removed children of mixed descent from their homes.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) stolen generations (ii) The native peoples of Australia, from the Latin 'ab origine', meaning 'from the beginning'. (iii) The government forcibly removed children of mixed descent from their homes.

items.stem: The fur most in demand from North America among European traders was that of the:
items.answer: beaver
items.markingKey: (d) beaver.
options: camel
elephant
tiger
beaver

items.stem:
Read the following statements about Europeans and the native peoples of North America:
I. The natives of North America claimed private ownership of land.
II. The fur trade with Europeans led to excessive hunting of animals like the beaver.
III. Europeans described natives as uncivilised, while natives saw Europeans as greedy.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: II and III only
items.markingKey: (c) I is incorrect: They did not claim ownership of land and used only what they needed. II is correct. III is correct.
options: I and II only
II only
II and III only
I only

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the native peoples of Australia and terra nullius is NOT correct?
items.answer: Captain James Cook reached Australia in 1788.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. Cook reached Botany Bay in 1770; the first convicts arrived in 1788.
options: Children of mixed descent were forcibly separated from their families, creating the 'stolen generations'.
The native peoples of Australia lived in many communities with their own languages and close links to the land.
Captain James Cook reached Australia in 1788.
The natives lost their land to sheep farms and later to mining and settlement.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about recognition of native rights in the twentieth century:
I. The Mabo judgement recognised that Aboriginal peoples had rights to their land before the British arrived.
II. The natives of the USA asserted their rights through the Declaration of Indian Rights in 1954.
III. From the 1970s, historians in Australia began to write about the history of the Aborigines.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: I and II only
I and III only
All of them
II only

items.stem: What is meant by 'Trail of Tears' in the context of natives and colonisers in the United States and Canada?
items.answer: The forced march of the Cherokee from their homeland, during which many died.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Trail of Tears correctly explained as the forced march of the Cherokee from their homeland, during which many died.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about natives and colonisers in the United States and Canada:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Neither I nor II
items.markingKey: (d) I is incorrect: Many Cherokee learnt English and tried to live like Americans, but were still evicted. II is incorrect: It bought Alaska from Russia in 1867.

II only
Both I and II

items.stem: "The British did not negotiate with the Aborigines for their land." Examine this statement with reference to the native peoples of Australia and terra nullius.
items.answer: The statement is valid. They claimed that Australia was terra nullius, empty land belonging to no one.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (they claimed that Australia was terra nullius, empty land belonging to no one.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Statement: The beaver population declined in North America.

items.answer: The fur trade with Europeans encouraged excessive hunting.
items.markingKey: (c) The fur trade with Europeans encouraged excessive hunting.
options: They wished to establish farms and settlements as private property.
The natives exchanged goods as gifts of friendship while the Europeans traded to make profits.
The fur trade with Europeans encouraged excessive hunting.
Thousands of newcomers poured into native lands in search of gold.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on natives and colonisers in the United States and Canada and answer the questions that follow.
"The USA expanded westward by purchase and war, buying Louisiana from France and Alaska from Russia. The railways helped settlers spread across the continent. The gold rush in California brought thousands of Europeans and others hoping to make a fortune."
(i) The Chief Justice of the US Supreme Court who ruled that the Cherokee were a distinct community was: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'gold rush' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Natives lost most of their land in the USA. (2)
items.answer: (i) John Marshall (ii) The rush of people to California after gold was discovered there, which brought more settlers to native lands. (iii) Settlers, gold seekers and railways spread westward and the government moved natives to reservations.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) John Marshall (ii) The rush of people to California after gold was discovered there, which brought more settlers to native lands. (iii) Settlers, gold seekers and railways spread westward and the government moved natives to reservations.

items.stem: The following statement about recognition of native rights in the twentieth century is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Native peoples of North America accepted their loss of land without protest."
items.answer: They protested and asserted their rights, as in the Declaration of Indian Rights of 1954.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (They protested and asserted their rights, as in the Declaration of Indian Rights of 1954.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The railways helped settlers spread across the continent. The democratic rights in the US Constitution, including the right to property, were not extended to the natives. Natives were pushed westward and confined to reservations as settlers took their land. The Cherokee had learnt English and tried to live in the American way, but were still forced from their land."
(i) Explain the term 'reservation', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The gold rush hurt the natives. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Cherokee had refused to learn English or adopt any American ways." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) A small area of land set aside by the government for native peoples after they were removed from their lands. (ii) Thousands of newcomers poured into native lands in search of gold. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Many Cherokee learnt English and tried to live like Americans, but were still evicted.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) A small area of land set aside by the government for native peoples after they were removed from their lands. (ii) Thousands of newcomers poured into native lands in search of gold. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Many Cherokee learnt English and tried to live like Americans, but were still evicted.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about Europeans and the native peoples of North America is correct?
items.answer: The native peoples of North America lived in groups along river valleys and in forests and grasslands.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: They did not claim ownership of land and used only what they needed. Natives exchanged goods as gifts; Europeans traded for profit and wanted land. They were the original inhabitants; the name 'Indians' came from Columbus's mistake.

The native peoples of North America lived in groups along river valleys and in forests and grasslands.
Europeans and natives held the same views about land and trade.
The natives of North America came from India.
